report.source_text: MR image was obtained and showed a small spherical lesion at right subcortical occipital lobe showing different intensities (Fig. 2). Lesion was hypointense on T1-weighted image, hyperintense rim on T2-weighted image. Ring enhancement was noted on the contrast enhanced T1 and blooming artefact on SWI. These findings suggesting granular nodular stage. Other multiple singular lesions were seen at left juxtacortical temporal lobe, right juxtacortical parietal lobe and left thalamus showing different intensities (Figs. 3, and 4). Lesion was also hypointense on T1-weighted image with no signal on T2-weighted image, with blooming artefact on SWI which suggesting nodular calcified stage. No restricted area was seen within the lesion on DWI-ADC on both stages.

report.source_text: MR Spectroscopy was conducted (Fig. 5). Minor shift scale (approximately -0.5 ppm) was made based on major resonances of N-acetylaspartate (NAA), creatine (Cr), and choline (Cho) in the spectroscopy control from the normal parenchyma. Increase in lactate and decrease in choline and N-acetylaspartate were seen which suggesting diagnosis of an inflammatory lesion. Levels of NAA/Cr ratio (0.38) and Cho/Cr ratio (1.21) were seen to be below 1.5.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 71-year-old man presented with a 4-month history of intermittent headaches (responsive to analgesics) and abrupt vision loss, along with 1-year history of left extremity weakness following a prior stroke 1 year ago. Initial routine laboratory and immunoserology examinations were within normal limits, including negative HIV antibody testing. MRI brain on admission revealed multiple cystic lesions characteristic of neurocysticercosis: (1) a small spherical lesion at the right subcortical occipital lobe in the granular nodular stage, showing hypointense T1-weighted signal, hyperintense rim on T2-weighted image, ring enhancement on contrast-enhanced T1, and blooming artifact on susceptibility-weighted imaging (SWI); (2) multiple singular lesions at the left juxtacortical temporal lobe, right juxtacortical parietal lobe, and left thalamus in the nodular calcified stage, showing hypointense T1-weighted signal, no signal on T2-weighted image, and blooming artifact on SWI. No restricted diffusion was noted on DWI-ADC sequences. MR Spectroscopy demonstrated increased lactate and decreased choline and N-acetylaspartate (NAA/Cr ratio 0.38, Cho/Cr ratio 1.21), consistent with an inflammatory lesion. These imaging findings are pathognomonic for neurocysticercosis with lesions in different evolutionary stages.

Multiple lesions in left temporal, right parietal, and left thalamus in nodular calcified stage with blooming artifact on SWI
MR Spectroscopy showing increased lactate and decreased choline and NAA consistent with inflammatory lesion
Clinical presentation with headaches, vision loss, and neurological deficits consistent with CNS parasitic infection
Routine labs and immunoserology within normal limits, HIV negative

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: While patient had prior stroke 1 year ago, the current presentation with multiple cystic lesions in different evolutionary stages on MRI is inconsistent with acute ischemic or hemorrhagic stroke. The imaging pattern is characteristic of chronic parasitic infection rather than acute vascular event.

The presence of multiple lesions in different evolutionary stages (granular nodular and nodular calcified) with characteristic ring enhancement and blooming artifacts is more consistent with parasitic cysticercosis than primary or secondary malignancy.

While tuberculosis can present with similar symptoms, the characteristic imaging pattern of multiple cystic lesions in different stages with blooming artifacts on SWI is pathognomonic for neurocysticercosis rather than tuberculosis.
HIV antibody testing was negative, ruling out HIV-related opportunistic infections or malignancies.
